newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain savings banks deny eyeing Endesa core stake.
newsitem.headline: Spain savings banks deny eyeing Endesa core stake.

text.p: Several Spanish regional savings banks denied on Wednesday a report that they are negotiating with electricity group Endesa with a view to becoming core shareholders.
"We are not involved in any type of negotiations with Endesa," a spokesman for the biggest regional savings bank La Caixa told Reuters.
Officials at Caja de Madrid and Basque regional savings bank Kutxa also denied talks. Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa (BBK) declined to comment.
A report in the ABC newspaper said four savings banks had for weeks been discussing the possibility of buying a core stake in Endesa, of which up to 33 percent is due to be privatised in the autumn.
The report said the only thing holding the banks back was Endesa's share price, which is at an all-time high.

Last week Endesa's chairman Rodolfo Martin Villa said he would prefer savings banks with an interest in Endesa subsidiaries to participate via the parent company, maintaining representation on the regional firms' boards.

Recently Endesa's share price has risen sharply, although analysts say there is no fundamental reason to justify the move. Some say the only explanation could be that a large investor is taking a key stake.

Endesa has risen from 10,970 pesetas ($74.35) at the close on June 17 to 12,920 pesetas at Tuesday's close. At 1030 GMT on Wednesday the stock was up a further 1.63 percent to 13,130 pesetas, versus an Ibex-35 blue chip index rise of 0.68 percent.

However, traded volume in Endesa has not been significant, and some dealers attribute the strong share price rise simply to a lack of sellers in the market. Furthermore, some chartists say short term Endesa is in free-rise.
